title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(藤本雅則研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Fujimoto Masanori)
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Acquire sufficient understanding and application specialized subjects related to the technical support required for research, development, design, and manufacture. (2) Acquire technical writing skills. (3) Learn how to create presentation materials and presentation scripts. (4) Learn about the importance of working with the community.
advice: We will cover the following topics: mechanical engineering, thermal engineering, manufacturing, design, and regional cooperation. Students are required to actively participate in class. Students are expected to check for various messages and materials in class.
requiredKnowledge: Preview and review related specialized subjects. Create and submit technical preparatory reports before each experimental class. Basic knowledge of related specialized subjects. Know how to use a calculator and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint).

activityGoals.body: Be able to act on a project theme using the engineering design process.
Be able to write down your achievements and discuss them in presentations.
Be able to act independently on other items presented separately.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) The purpose and advancement process of a project theme are accurately understood, and the annual goal established for the purpose can be achieved. The process can also be reported in the Design Project Activity Support System or on paper. (2) Interim results from the implementation of the project can be compiled into the interim report, which can be presented and discussed. The final results can be compiled into the final report, which can be presented and discussed at the Design Project III. (3) If necessary, students can design and manufacture their own products, and the performance of the products can be evaluated.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) The purpose and advancement process of one project theme are accurately understood, and the annual goal established for the purpose can be achieved. The process can also be recorded in the Design Project III Activity Support System or on paper. (2) Interim results from the execution of the project can be compiled into the interim report and the content of the report can be released. The final results can be compiled into the final report and presented at the Design Project III. (3) If necessary, students can design and manufacture products by hand.

lessons.content: April: Orientation Safety education (including handling of experimental equipment) Review the content of the special seminar and review the literature on each research theme determined by the special seminar
May: Thematic discussions Realization of research themes
June: Thematic discussions Preliminary study of each research theme Review existing literature and confirm of reproducibility
July: Thematic discussions Examination and promotion of feasibility of each research theme
August: Thematic discussions Interim report meeting Pursuit of each research theme
September: Thematic discussions Pursuit of each research theme
October: Thematic discussions Pursuit of each research theme
November: Thematic discussions Pursuit of each research theme
December: Thematic discussions Interim report meeting Project reporting Pursuit of each research theme
January: Thematic discussions Project reporting Pursuit of each research theme
February: Public screening presentation Project reporting Preparation of presentation materials
